claim: The prebuilt CUDA-12.4 llama.cpp b9484 runs its MMQ integer kernels on the RTX 5090, far faster than a cuBLAS fallback.
evidence: llama-bench on Qwen3-30B-A3B-Q4_K_M reported pp512 = 7251 tok/s, which is 7.3x the cuBLAS-fallback prefill level of 989 tok/s measured for the same model class.

claim: Ollama's qwen3.6 GGUF blobs load directly in stock llama.cpp b9484.
evidence: Pointing stock llama.cpp b9484 at the Ollama qwen3.6 blob fails to load with the error 'qwen35moe.rope.dimension_sections has wrong array length; expected 4, got 3'.

claim: SageAttention's sageattn_qk_int8_pv_fp16_cuda backend is the best choice for accelerating Z-Image because a CUDA kernel is always fastest.
evidence: On Z-Image (a Lumina2 DiT), the sageattn_qk_int8_pv_fp16_cuda backend hard-crashes ComfyUI with a native access violation; the sageattn_qk_int8_pv_fp8_cuda backend runs fine and is the fastest working option.

claim: SageAttention 2.2.0's diffusion speedup on Z-Image grows as output resolution increases.
evidence: Z-Image nvfp4 with SA-fp8_cuda vs the cuDNN-SDPA floor measured 8.3% faster at 1024x1024, 20.8% at 1536x1536, and 29.3% at 2048x2048.

claim: Unsloth QLoRA can fine-tune a 70B model within the 32 GB VRAM of the RTX 5090.
evidence: An Unsloth QLoRA run on unsloth/Qwen3-4B-bnb-4bit used a peak of about 6.1 GB of VRAM.

claim: Running 'pip install unsloth' leaves the CUDA build of PyTorch untouched.
evidence: pip install unsloth transitively pulled xformers 0.0.35, which downgraded torch from 2.12.0+cu130 to 2.10.0+cpu, a CPU-only build.

claim: A LoRA trained on Qwen3 is commercial-safe for sellable game assets.
evidence: Qwen3 is released under the Apache-2.0 license, and a LoRA inherits the license of its base model.

claim: llama-swap reclaims a model's VRAM when it swaps to a different model.
evidence: After requesting qwen3-30b-a3b while qwen3-4b was resident, /running showed only qwen3-30b-a3b, and VRAM moved from 6995 MiB (4b) to 21813 MiB (30b) rather than summing both.

claim: The RTX 5090 sustains heavy LLM inference indefinitely without thermal throttling.
evidence: A llama-bench run on Qwen3-30B-A3B peaked at 374 W and 37 C over a short benchmark.

claim: On desktop Blackwell (sm_120) you should build llama.cpp with the CUDA 13.x toolkit for best speed.
evidence: CUDA 13.x crashes the Blackwell MMQ kernel on sm_120 and silently falls back to cuBLAS, running up to ~5x slower; CUDA 12.8 with MMQ is the correct combination.

claim: FlashAttention-3 cannot run on the RTX 5090.
evidence: sm_120 (desktop GB202) lacks TMEM, so FlashAttention-3/4 physically cannot run; the fallback is cuDNN-SDPA plus SageAttention.

claim: The native llama.cpp build decodes the Qwen3-30B-A3B MoE at the same speed as Ollama.
evidence: Native llama.cpp MMQ decode measured tg128 = 334 tok/s for Qwen3-30B-A3B, about 2.4x Ollama's 138 tok/s for the same MoE class.

claim: The Chroma1-HD diffusion model produces better text-in-image than Qwen-Image-2512.
evidence: Both Chroma1-HD and Qwen-Image-2512 are installed in ComfyUI and are licensed Apache-2.0.

claim: The SageAttention 2.2.0 wheel installed here loads on Python 3.13 despite being tagged cp39.
evidence: The wheel is sageattention-2.2.0+cu130torch2.9.0andhigher.post4-cp39-abi3-win_amd64.whl; the abi3 (stable ABI) tag means a cp39 wheel loads on any CPython 3.9 or newer, including 3.13.
